title: erlang.config.json
description: How ERLANG scans a subject, read from the scan root only (lib/scope.js). Every report names the config, what it excludes, the handlers it names and the tables it calls small.

exclude.description: Paths relative to the scan root that are not part of the app, such as test fixtures with planted defects or generated reports. A directory (trailing / optional) excludes everything under it; a file excludes that file. No globs, no .., nothing absolute.

handlers.description: Request handlers ERLANG cannot find in the source, or entry points that are not HTTP routes (a queue consumer, a job). Each names a function by its name in a file; its code, and what it calls, is in the request path for the checks that judge what a request costs (lib/handlers.js). An entry that names nothing is a note in the report.

file.description: Relative to the scan root, with / separators.

function.description: A function declared in the file, by name.

method.description: The HTTP method, or the operation in capitals for other protocols.

route.description: A route template, such as /orders/:id; for a queue, its name.

smallTables.description: Tables (or Prisma models) the owner states stay small, such as settings or country codes: reading all of their rows is not reported by unbounded-query. Every report names them.

database.description: The database the deployed processes share, as its owner states it. pool-sizing compares every pool's connections against maxConnections less the 3 PostgreSQL reserves for superusers; without it, a managed database's limit is unknown and the finding is info.

maxConnections.description: PostgreSQL's max_connections, as set on the server (SHOW max_connections).

warmup.description: A cheap route the trace harness requests once in each fresh process before it times first requests (cold-start, STB-10), such as a health check that reads once through the app's database driver. It takes up the start-up cost every first request pays (the framework's first dispatch, the driver's first query, the runtime's work after listen), so a route is judged on its own set-up only. Without it the harness requests a path that does not exist and expects a 404, which warms the framework but not the database driver; every report says which warm-up ran.

method.description: GET (the default) or HEAD: the warm-up must not change anything.

path.description: A path on the app itself, starting with a single /; no host.
